\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Threshold Functions --- Gaussian}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Gaussian
\section{Overview}
The quantitative Gaussian approximation statements and correlated-Gaussian quadrant formula lead to regular-threshold and majority noise-stability bounds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Kolmogorov distance of real measures]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.kolmogorovDistance}
\leanok
For measures $\mu,\nu$ on $\mathbb R$, define $D_K(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\mu(({-\infty},t])-\nu(({-\infty},t])|$, taking the real value of each measure mass, assigning real value zero to infinite mass, and assigning supremum zero if the displayed set is unbounded. For probability measures this is the usual Kolmogorov distance.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universal third-moment Gaussian approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.berryEsseen}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.kolmogorovDistance, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
There exists a universal real constant $c\ge0$ such that, for every $n\ge0$ and family of independent measurable real random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ on any probability space, if each $|X_i|^3$ is integrable, $\mathbb E X_i=0$, and $\sum_i\mathbb E X_i^2=1$, then $D_K(\mathcal L(\sum_iX_i),\gamma)\le c\sum_i\mathbb E|X_i|^3$. Here $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian measure and $D_K(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\mu(({-\infty},t])-\nu(({-\infty},t])|$ for probability measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute first moment of a regular sign sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.rademacher_abs_expectation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ such that for every $n\ge0$, real coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, and real $\varepsilon$, if $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for all $i$, then $|\mathbb E|\sum_i a_i\xi_i|-\sqrt{2/\pi}|\le C\varepsilon$, where the $\xi_i$ are independent uniform signs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Lower-left probability of a Gaussian pair]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianQuadrantProbability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
Let $G,H$ be independent standard real Gaussians. For every real $\rho$, define $Q(\rho)=\Pr[G\le0,\ \rho G+\sqrt{\max(1-\rho^2,0)}\,H\le0]$; when $|\rho|\le1$, the two displayed coordinates form a standard Gaussian pair of correlation $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sheppard formula for a Gaussian quadrant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sheppard_formula}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.angular_measure_two_halfplanes, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianQuadrantProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussian_cone_lintegral, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussian_prod_apply, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.measurableSet_twoHalfplaneAngles, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G,H$ be independent standard real Gaussians and let $-1\le\rho\le1$. Then $\Pr[G\le0,\ \rho G+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,H\le0]=\tfrac12-\arccos(\rho)/(2\pi)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian approximation for regular threshold stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.regular_ltf_stability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsHomogeneousLinearThresholdRepresentation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability}
There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ with the following property. For every $n\ge0$, real coefficients $a_i$, and real $\varepsilon,\rho$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, $|\rho|<1$, and $\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\ne0$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $f(x)$ equal $1$ when $\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\ge0$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then $|\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)-(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho|\le C\sqrt{\max(\varepsilon,0)}/(1-\rho)$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority stability decreases to the Gaussian limit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_stability_limit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_noiseStability_antitone, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.majority}
There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ such that for every $0\le\rho<1$, the majority function $M_k$ on $2k+1$ uniform bits, equal to $1$ when $\sum_i(-1)^{x_i}>0$ and $-1$ otherwise, satisfies $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_{k+1})\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)$ for all $k\ge0$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)\to(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho$ as $k\to\infty$. For every integer $k\ge0$, $(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)\le(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho+C/(\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\sqrt{2k+1})$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Small-influence upper bound on noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_is_stablest}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.maxInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
For every $0<\rho<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\tau>0$ such that for all $n\ge0$ and $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ with uniform mean zero and $I_i(f)\le\tau$ for every $i$, one has $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)\le(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho+\varepsilon$. Here $I_i(f)=\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^{\{i\}}))^2]/4$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}
